SQL:
SELECT
  customers__regions.name AS "orders.customers.regions.name",
  DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date) AS "orders.order_date",
  CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
FROM orders AS orders
LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
  ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
LEFT JOIN regions AS customers__regions
  ON customers.region_id = customers__regions.id
WHERE
  (
    orders.order_date >= CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND orders.order_date < CAST('2025-04-01' AS DATE)
  )
GROUP BY
  customers__regions.name,
  DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date)
ORDER BY
  "orders.order_date" ASC,
  "orders.customers.regions.name" ASC

args.message: I split the saved monthly_rev query (total order amount per month) by region for January–March 2025, linking each order to its customer and then to the customer's region. Every Q1 2025 order has a known region, so there is no "unknown region" group in this period. The table has 12 rows: 3 months × 4 regions (East, North, South, West). Some orders in other periods do lack a region (16 orders, 1,193.30 in total), but none of them fall in Q1 2025. The regions add up exactly to the saved query's monthly totals: January 10,070.12, February 8,920.94, March 9,816.20.
